name: Sheshbazzar
title: Levite and Law Interpreter
summary: Sheshbazzar was a Levite who served in Jerusalem after the return from exile in Babylon. He was involved in the matter of mixed marriages and helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it aloud. He is mentioned several times in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah as one of the prominent Levites of this period.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Matter of Mixed Marriages
keyEvents.description: Sheshbazzar was among those involved in addressing the issue of Israelite men marrying foreign women, although some sources suggest he opposed the process.

keyEvents.title: Help with Explaining the Law
keyEvents.description: Sheshbazzar was among the Levites who helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it aloud to the assembly.

keyEvents.title: Overseeing the External Work at God's House
keyEvents.description: Sheshbazzar was responsible for the external work at God's house, which involved practical administration of temple affairs.

keyEvents.title: Participation in Ezra's Reforms
keyEvents.description: As a prominent Levite, Shabbethai actively participated in the religious reforms carried out by Ezra and Nehemiah to restore proper worship in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Service Among the Levites in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Shabbethai was counted among the leading Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the rebuilding of the wall and played a central role in organizing temple service.
